summary: Identity-proxy claim normalization strips Okta externalId with invisible chars, blocking temporary support token issuance
summary_template: Identity-proxy is removing group/externalId claim when it contains non-printable unicode sequences, which prevents the support issuance flow from finding entitlements and causes 401 on support-tool token request
description:
Issue summary: When Okta profiles contain externalId/group names with invisible or non-printable Unicode characters (e.g. ZERO WIDTH JOINER U+200D) the identity-proxy normalization layer strips the claim. The support token service relies on the presence of that claim to issue temporary support tokens for the internal jumpbox/runbook workflow. Impact: internal support engineers cannot generate temporary support tokens for affected users; attempts return 401 Unauthorized from /api/v1/support/tokens. The problem is intermittent because not all Okta profiles have the invisible char and some proxy routes use a different normalization config.

Impact: Multiple oncall engineers reported inability to elevate for urgent runbook work (approx 6 incidents in the last 24h). This blocks emergency access and delays incident response.

Environment: prod (us-east, identity-proxy cluster id ipx-prod-3).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use an Okta profile where group externalId contains a zero-width joiner or non-printable char (example: "oncall\u200dcontractor:eng").
2) Login via SSO to the internal console and request a temporary support token via the support-tool UI.
3) Observe support-tool backend calling identity-proxy for claims; identity-proxy returns payload without the affected group claim.
4) Support-tool responds 401 because entitlement check failed.

Expected: identity-proxy should forward claims unmodified (or document/destructure) so entitlement service can make a decision.

Relevant logs/traces:
- support-tool request id: st-20260310-7a1b2c
- identity-proxy trace id: ipx-trace-0a9f3d
- Example JWT payload observed (before normalization): 
  header: {alg: RS256}
  payload: {"sub":"u-2345","groups":["eng:platform","oncall\u200dcontractor:eng"]}
- Example returned payload after normalization (identity-proxy): {"sub":"u-2345","groups":["eng:platform"]}

Related ops artifacts: linked PR to identity-proxy library that introduced normalization: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1540
Confluence runbook reference: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/support-token-issuance
steps_to_reproduce: Provision an Okta test user with group externalId containing U+200D (zero-width joiner)
SAML/SSO login via electron console to ensure same header route as support-tool
Trigger support-tool token issuance from the UI and capture trace ids
Inspect identity-proxy logs for trace id ipx-trace-* and compare inbound vs outbound JWT payloads
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Reported first observed at 2026-03-10 09:34 UTC. Affected users are internal engineers with contractor tags. Attached debug traces.
Rafael Ortega (Identity): Assigned to investigate. Noted similar normalization change in PR #1540 that canonicalizes group strings by stripping control characters. Will reproduce locally.
Jamie Patel (SRE): Observed increased 401 rate on support-tool /api/v1/support/tokens between 09:00-11:00 UTC; correlated with ipx-prod-3 proxy restarts at 08:52 UTC after deploy.

Rafael Ortega (Identity) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reproduction with test user. Identity-proxy's sanitizer uses "[\x00-\x1F\x7F]+" which removes U+200D because of incorrect unicode class handling in Go string normalization library. Preparing hotfix.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Temporary workaround used: issued admin token via admin console for six incidents; documented manual steps in ticket.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: recent change to identity-proxy's claim sanitizer (PR #1540) attempted to remove non-printable ASCII control chars but unexpectedly removed certain unicode codepoints when run through the current unicode normalization function.

Reproduced locally by creating JWT with group value containing U+200D; sanitized result strips the entire group name instead of only control bytes. Unit tests for unicode handling missing for non-ASCII invisible characters.
SRE noted that only ipx-prod-3 had the new binary; ipx-prod-{1,2} were still on previous version and did not show the issue, explaining intermittent nature.

Auth team identified the sanitization function path: internal/normalizer/strip_control_chars.go:NormalizeClaims. The regex uses \x classes instead of unicode package and is causing the drop for codepoints > 0x7F when combined with multi-byte rune handling.
workarounds: Manual admin token issuance via console for affected users (runbook: support-token-issuance, section 'admin-override')
Roll back identity-proxy to previous binary on ipx-prod-3 to restore behavior while hotfix prepared
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC: Deployed hotfix build identity-proxy v2.4.2 to ipx-prod-3 that changes NormalizeClaims to use unicode.IsControl(rune) checks instead of "\x00-\x1F" regex. This preserves visible and non-visible unicode codepoints that are valid group names.
Verification: Re-run reproduction steps and confirmed support-tool token issuance succeeds for test users with U+200D in group externalId. Monitored 2 hours; 401 rate returned to baseline.
Post-deploy: Added unit tests covering ZWJ U+200D, ZWNJ U+200C, and other common invisible characters. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1572 merged.

Follow-up: Confluence runbook updated with note to include unicode invisible-character checks when adding claim sanitizers. Engineering action: add canary rollout policy for identity-proxy changes to avoid single-cluster exposure.
next_steps: Backfill unit tests for any other sanitizer functions across identity-proxy and identity-service
Schedule a short postmortem meeting with Identity, SRE, and Support to review rollout practices (owner: Rafael Ortega)
Add a synthetic check to our global SLOs that runs support-token-issuance flow once per region per deploy to catch regressions earlier
